## 0. Decisions (recorded)

- **D1 — Hosted-origin CI deploy + compose CORS default: DESCOPED.** The
  hosting provider for `app.openpalm.dev` is TBD outside the repo (assessment
  risk 1; plan §12.3 item 3 "hosting provider TBD") — a deploy job needs a real
  target, credentials, and DNS none of which exist. The milestone plan's
  cross-cutting decision already binds the compose CORS default to it:
  "`https://app.openpalm.dev` enters the compose CORS default only when the
  hosted deploy actually exists" (implementation-plan.md §Cross-cutting). Both
  items are descoped together and the decision is recorded in the docs this
  task updates (D7). Everything else in this task is built origin-agnostic
  (keyed on `location.origin` / connection URLs, no hosted-origin literals in
  product code) so the future deploy job is the ONLY missing piece for the
  phone path. Requirements for that future job are pinned in §6 (risk 2) so
  they are not lost.
- **D2 — Handshake is a new client leaf module, not a transport change.**
  `packages/client/src/lib/runtime-handshake.ts` (assessment offered
  `transport/index.ts` or a new module). The transport is scoped to a
  connection's OpenCode/guardian API surface; the handshake probes a different,
  OpenPalm-host contract (`/api/runtime` at the connection's **origin root**)
  and must treat "endpoint absent" as the normal legacy case, not an error.
  Keeping it a pure leaf module (injectable fetch, never throws) matches the
  `url-policy.ts` precedent and leaves the pinned transport contract untouched.
  Scope: the connections page runs it for `openpalm-client-api`-kind entries
  only (plain `remote-opencode` targets are by definition non-OpenPalm servers
  with nothing to handshake).
- **D3 — Pairing = self-contained signed-nothing payload, minted by the host
  app against the existing guardian principal API.** The host UI's
  `POST /api/connections/pairing` mints a `direct` principal via the guardian
  admin listener (`http://127.0.0.1:${OP_GUARDIAN_ADMIN_PORT:-3831}`) — the
  exact flow `docs/managing-openpalm.md` documents manually — and returns a
  one-time-displayed pairing code (`openpalm-pair:` + base64url JSON
  `{v:1, kind, url, label, username, secret}`) rendered as QR + copyable
  string. The client parses the code and **pre-fills the existing add form**
  (secret flows through the existing `buildAuth()` → encrypted secret store
  path; the stored `ConnectionEntry` carries only `secretRef`). Explicit
  non-goal, recorded: a server-mediated short-lived claim/exchange endpoint —
  it would add a new unauthenticated guardian ingress surface (#435-scale
  review burden) for marginal gain; the payload's `v` field keeps the format
  evolvable if that ever ships. "One-time" semantics: the code is displayed
  once and never persisted host-side; the durable artifact is the revocable
  guardian principal (`DELETE /admin/principals/:id`, #433).
- **D4 — Mint orchestration lives in `@openpalm/lib`; the client gets a twin
  decoder.** Encoding + principal minting is portable control-plane logic
  (core-principles §Shared control-plane library — a future `openpalm pair`
  CLI command must not duplicate it), so
  `packages/lib/src/control-plane/pairing.ts` owns
  `encodePairingCode`/`decodePairingCode`/`mintDirectPrincipalPairingCode`,
  and the ui route is a thin transport wrapper. `packages/client` NEVER
  imports `@openpalm/lib` (purity gate), so it carries a ~25-line twin
  `parsePairingCode` — the established twin pattern
  (`normalizeGuardianUrl` client / `normalizeGuardianOcUrl` ui server, #486
  D2), pinned compatible by a client test that imports the lib encoder
  **tests-only** (precedent: `tests/remote-attach.e2e.test.ts:58` imports
  `../../guardian/src/oc-doc-fixture.ts`; `purity.test.ts` scans only `src/`
  and `build/`).
- **D5 — One new dependency: `uqr` (called out per the no-unjustified-complexity
  rule).** QR generation has NO Bun/Web built-in; the alternatives are an
  in-repo Reed-Solomon + masking encoder (~400 lines of untouchable complexity)
  or an external image service (leaks the credential). `uqr@0.1.3` is
  zero-dependency, MIT, typed ESM, exports `renderSVG(text)` (verified against
  the published tarball), and goes in `packages/ui` **devDependencies** (the ui
  package's house pattern — it has no runtime `dependencies`; adapter-node
  inlines devDeps like `markdown-it`/`croner`). Rendering happens server-side
  in the pairing route (SVG string in the JSON response), so `uqr` never enters
  a browser bundle and never touches `packages/client`. Installed once via
  root `bun install` (single-lockfile rule).
- **D6 — Pairing endpoint capability = `host:stack:write` (not
  `connections:manage`).** Minting writes a principal into the LOCAL stack's
  guardian — a host-stack mutation. `connections:manage` is advertised in
  `pwa-static` mode (stack-less `openpalm app`), where there is no local
  guardian to mint against and the endpoint must not exist; `host:stack:write`
  is exact (electron-host/host-ui only) and needs no new capability name.
  Enforced server-side via `requireCapability()` (`$lib/server/helpers.ts:130`)
  **plus** the admin session + origin check via `withAdminBody()` — the same
  double guard as sibling `/api/connections` writes. The host-page button is
  `hasCapability('host:stack:write')`-gated (UX only, per §8.5).
- **D7 — Descope + close-out recording.** `docs/technical/ui-runtime-modes.md`
  "Not Yet Shipped" keeps ONLY the hosted-origin deploy entry (annotated with
  the D1 rationale + the CORS-default coupling) and drops the
  pairing/handshake/affordance entries this task ships;
  `ui-runtime-modes-plan.md` §12.3 statuses updated the same way;
  `managing-openpalm.md` gains the pairing-UI path as the primary flow with
  the manual mint kept as the advanced/headless alternative; CHANGELOG
  `[Unreleased]` entry added. This satisfies the milestone exit criterion
  "explicitly descoped with a recorded decision".
- **D8 — `clientAppUrl` is an additive optional field on
  `ServerRuntimeContext`;** `version` stays `2` (additive fields are exactly
  the compatible evolution the handshake's `compatible` state promises).
  Computed for `electron-host`/`host-ui`/`pwa-static` from lib's
  `resolveClientAppPort(process.env)` (`client-app-url.ts:3-5`; Electron
  already merges `stack.env` into the ui child env, `main.ts:255-272`);
  omitted in `assistant-container`. The host-page "Install OpenPalm app"
  button renders only after a browser-side `no-cors` reachability probe
  succeeds (the E4 dead-link lesson from Electron's `openLocalApp()`).

descoped with D1 (additionally untestable end-to-end until a TLS-fronted
guardian exists in a real deployment — assessment risk 3). All other criteria
are closed or already closed (§4).

## 3. File-level changes

### packages/lib

- **CREATE `packages/lib/src/control-plane/pairing.ts`**
  ```ts
  export type PairingPayloadV1 = {
    v: 1;
    kind: 'openpalm-client-api';
    url: string;        // operator-entered guardian base URL (client normalizes /oc on save)
    label?: string;
    username: string;   // minted principal id
    secret: string;     // minted principal token
  };
  export const PAIRING_CODE_PREFIX = 'openpalm-pair:';
  export function encodePairingCode(payload: PairingPayloadV1): string;      // prefix + base64url(JSON) via Buffer 'base64url'
  export type DecodePairingResult = { ok: true; payload: PairingPayloadV1 } | { ok: false; error: string };
  export function decodePairingCode(code: string): DecodePairingResult;      // prefix optional; strict field validation; never throws
  export type MintPairingResult =
    | { ok: true; code: string; principalId: string }
    | { ok: false; error: string };
  export function mintDirectPrincipalPairingCode(options: {
    homeDir: string;
    label: string;
    url: string;
    guardianAdminUrl?: string;            // default 'http://127.0.0.1:3831'
    fetchImpl?: typeof fetch;             // injectable for tests
  }): Promise<MintPairingResult>;
  ```
  Behavior: validate `url` parses as http(s); read the admin token via
  `readSecret(homeDir, 'op_guardian_admin_token')` (fail closed with a
  structured error naming the secret when absent); token = 32 random bytes hex
  via Web Crypto (`crypto.getRandomValues`); `principalId` =
  slug(label) (lowercase, `[^a-z0-9]+`→`-`, trimmed, ≤24 chars) + `-` + 4 hex
  chars; `POST ${guardianAdminUrl}/admin/principals` with
  `authorization: Bearer <token>`, body `{id, kind:'direct', token, label}`
  (contract: `packages/guardian/src/admin.ts:66-76`); non-2xx/network error →
  `{ok:false}`. Never log the secret (structured `createLogger` use only for
  non-secret events, per bunjs-rules §4 — or no logging at all).

  `encodePairingCode`, `decodePairingCode`, `mintDirectPrincipalPairingCode`,
  `PAIRING_CODE_PREFIX`, and the three types, alongside the existing

  ```ts
  export const SUPPORTED_RUNTIME_CONTRACT_VERSION = 2; // mirrors packages/ui/src/lib/types.ts:36-37 (pinned by T7)
  export type RuntimeContractResult =
    | { state: 'compatible'; version: number }
    | { state: 'newer'; version: number }     // server > supported
    | { state: 'older'; version: number }     // server < supported
    | { state: 'legacy' };                    // endpoint absent/unreadable — plain OpenCode/guardian
  export async function checkRuntimeContract(
    connectionUrl: string,
    fetchImpl: typeof globalThis.fetch = globalThis.fetch
  ): Promise<RuntimeContractResult>;
  ```
  Behavior: `new URL('/api/runtime', connectionUrl)` (origin root); GET with
  `credentials:'omit'`, `cache:'no-store'` (SW bypass — vite.config.ts:77
  no-store exclusion), `AbortSignal.timeout(5000)`; any non-2xx, network
  error, non-JSON body, or missing/non-integer `version` → `{state:'legacy'}`.
  Never throws (graceful degradation is the contract — assessment risk 4).

  ```ts
  export type PairingPayload = { v: 1; kind: 'openpalm-client-api'; url: string; label?: string; username: string; secret: string };
  export type ParsePairingResult = { ok: true; payload: PairingPayload } | { ok: false; error: string };
  export function parsePairingCode(code: string): ParsePairingResult;
  ```
  base64url decode via `atob` + `Uint8Array` + `TextDecoder` (UTF-8-safe —
  same rationale as transport `base64Utf8`, transport/index.ts:216-227);
  optional `openpalm-pair:` prefix; strict validation; never throws; never
  logs the secret.

## 5. Verification gates (implementer runs ALL green, in order)

```bash
bun install                                   # once, repo root — new uqr dep (single-lockfile rule)
bun run lint                                  # Biome, repo-wide
bun run check                                 # svelte-check: ui + ui-kit + client
bun run client:build && bun run client:test   # build FIRST — purity gate + pwa-config need build/
bun run ui:check
bun run electron:test                         # must stay green with zero electron changes
bun run lib:test                              # new lib pairing suite
cd packages/ui && npm run test:unit -- --run --project server   # node-project vitest (browser project is proxy-blocked in the dev container, plan §12.6)
cd packages/client && bun run test:browsers && bun run test:e2e # T11; if the sandbox blocks the browser download, CI's client-browser-tests job (ci.yml:355) is the enforcing gate — say so in the PR-stage report
bun run test                                  # full aggregate (client first, then sdk/guardian/portals/cli/lib/ui-kit/electron-tools/scripts)
```

Baseline rule: compare any lib root-uid ownership flakes against the
pre-change baseline (implementation-plan.md, known sandbox flakes).

## 6. Risks and how the design avoids them (from the assessment)

1. **Hosting provider TBD** → descoped (D1) with a recorded decision; nothing
   in this task hardcodes the hosted origin (grep-clean product code; the only
   `app.openpalm.dev` literals stay in tests/docs).
2. **SW precache pinning on the hosted origin** → travels with the descoped
   deploy job. Pinned requirement for that future job (recorded here so it is
   not lost): the host must serve `index.html`/`sw.js`/`registerSW.js` with
   `no-cache` semantics mirroring `bin/serve.mjs`
   (`packages/client/tests/serve.test.ts:150-172`), hashed `_app/immutable/*`
   long-lived, and no `runtime-config.json` at the hosted root. This task
   changes no cache semantics anywhere.
3. **Phone criterion untestable until #557-style TLS fronting exists in a real
   deployment** → phone criterion descoped with D1; everything shippable is
   verified headless (unit + Playwright against the real build).
4. **`/api/runtime` absent on plain OpenCode/guardian bases** → `legacy` is a
   first-class non-error state, test-pinned (T7 rows 4–6); the page renders
   nothing for it; the handshake runs only for `openpalm-client-api` kinds.
5. **Pairing = new credential-issuance surface** → no new listener and no new
   protocol: minting reuses the guardian's existing loopback-only,
   Bearer-gated admin API (#435 coordination satisfied — no parallel
   mechanism); the endpoint is double-guarded (`host:stack:write` capability +
   admin session + origin check, T3 rows 2–3); the token is generated with Web
   Crypto, never logged, never persisted host-side, returned only inside the
   one-time code; the client stores it via the EXISTING encrypted secret store
   and the connection record carries only `secretRef` (T9 + existing
   `connections-secrets.test.ts` contract); `?pair=` is stripped from history
   (T10 row 2); principals are individually revocable
   (`DELETE /admin/principals/:id`, #433). QR is rendered locally by `uqr` —
   no external service ever sees the payload.
6. **CORS default touches every install** → untouched (descoped with D1); the
   already-shipped loopback-only default stays as-is; the pairing endpoint's
   `warnings` + panel copy tell the operator exactly which env keys to set
   instead of the stack mutating them implicitly (posture unchanged:
   loopback-default binds, `GUARDIAN_DIRECT_INGRESS` stays default-off).
7. **New-dependency risk (uqr)** → zero-dependency, MIT, typed, verified
   published API (`renderSVG`), pinned exact `0.1.3`, devDependencies of
   packages/ui only, server-side use only — never in the client artifact
   (purity gate unaffected).

## 7. Out of scope (explicit)

- Hosted-origin CI deploy job + `app.openpalm.dev` in the compose CORS default
  (D1 — external infrastructure; recorded decision).
- "Phone: install from the official hosted URL" acceptance criterion (blocked
  on the above + a real TLS-fronted guardian).
- Serving `/api/runtime` from the guardian or the assistant-container static
  co-process (Slice B settings shim, plan §6.9 item 6 — optional, unbuilt by
  its own gating; the client handshake degrades gracefully without it).
- In-client camera scanning (`BarcodeDetector`) — not universally available;
  "scan" is served by the OS camera / any QR reader decoding the code (+ the
  `?pair=` deep link for a future hosted origin), then paste.
- A server-mediated short-lived pairing claim/exchange endpoint (D3 non-goal).
- Electron changes of any kind (affordance shipped; tray/menu untouched).
- B15 in-chat connection switcher, voice port (B10), `channel_lan` &c. —
  other issues' scope (§12.7).
- Renaming/retiring `requiresHttpsForRemoteConnections` in
  `packages/ui/src/lib/server/features.ts:130` — it is served in the runtime
  context consumed by #557's client-side enforcement; no change needed here.
